newsitem.title: USA: US troubled by reports of aid to Zaire rebels.
newsitem.headline: US troubled by reports of aid to Zaire rebels.

text.p: The United States is troubled by reports that rebels in Zaire are getting help and weapons from the governments of neighbouring Uganda, Burundi, Rwanda and Angola, the State Department said on Monday.

"This is an extremely troubling development ... that Zaire is threatened on all sides," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told a briefing. "The territorial integrity of Zaire, its sovereignty, is terribly important for stability throughout Central Africa," he said.
"We're still concerned by the flood of reports that there is assistance flowing to the rebels by the government in Uganda and also the governments in Burundi and Rwanda."
Burns said Washington had raised this issue with these three governments, but added: "I can't say that we're satisfied with what we see happening on the ground."
In addition, he said the United States was concerned "by men in arms coming across the Angolan-Zairean border."
Burns' comments followed the rebel takeover on Saturday of Zaire's third largest city, Kisangani. The central government based at Kinshasa told its citizens not to panic despite the military defeat.

Burns reiterated U.S. calls for a ceasefire and negotiations between the Kinshasa government and the rebels, but also said: "The fall of Kisangani over the weekend is an extremely troubling indicator of instability in Zaire."

Tutsi-led rebels took up arms in October, vowing to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko. They accused Zairean authorities of denying them citizenship and planning to expel them to Rwanda, their ancestral home.
